2016.analyst_notes: Warm, employee-centered storytelling with quantified volunteering and giving figures ($41M contributed, 329,000+ volunteer hours), but no environmental or sustainability content appears on the Culture page; that topic is left to the separate Corporate Responsibility report.

2017.change_reason: New headline ('our employees put values into action'), new stories (Luanda malaria painting, Thai conservation project, Houston pro bono legal work), and 2016 impact figures ($38M, 9,300+ volunteers) replace the 2015 content, while the page structure is unchanged.
2017.analyst_notes: Environmental content is limited to one clause about natural-resource conservation in a Thai volunteer project. The framing stays volunteer-centered rather than a sustainability commitment.

2018.change_reason: Adds a 'Day in the Life' series of employee profiles (firefighter, ship captain, data scientist), STEM outreach, and 2017 impact figures ($33.1M, 8,010+ volunteers), along with new environmental items such as whooping crane habitat work.
2018.analyst_notes: The 'Human Energy' and 'ingenuity' language is aspirational and people-focused. Environmental items (tree planting, habitat work in Louisiana) are brief and presented as community service rather than operational performance.

2019.change_reason: Replaces the earlier stories with international volunteering in Kazakhstan, the Philippines (2.4 tons of coastal litter removed), Singapore, and Indonesia, plus a Trees For Houston partnership (225,000+ trees planted cumulatively) and 2018 impact figures ($35.2M, 274,200+ volunteer hours).
2019.analyst_notes: This is the most environment-leaning CVX capture (tree planting, coastal cleanup, sea turtles), but it is still reported as volunteer activity rather than as emissions or operational performance. The tree-planting figure is specific, while the framing is generic.

2020.change_reason: A new integrity block ('getting results the right way', 'a culture of integrity') appears, impact figures move to 2019 values ($36.7M, 7,752 people, 193,369 hours, down from 274,200), and report links are updated.
2020.analyst_notes: The integrity block is one generic sentence with a 'learn more about governance' link and no specifics. The drop in reported volunteer hours is not explained anywhere on the page.

2021.change_reason: Only small additions: a 30-year PRIDE anniversary block and updated report links, with the same stories and the same 2019 impact figures.
2021.analyst_notes: Content is largely identical to 2020, including duplicated caption text from scraping. The 2019 impact figures are carried forward, so the page is no longer reporting new numbers.

2022.change_reason: Only the report link labels change (to 2021); the copy and figures are otherwise identical to 2021.
2022.analyst_notes: Stories and impact figures remain at 2019 data, so the page is effectively static on this topic.

2023.change_reason: Copy is essentially identical to 2022, with minor layout and link changes and report links moved to 2022.
2023.analyst_notes: No new stories or metrics appear; the culture narrative and its statistics are unchanged across four captures.

2024.change_reason: Essentially identical to 2023, with the same stories and 2019 impact figures; only minor text differences.
2024.analyst_notes: From 2020 through 2024 the page reports the same 2019 metrics, which suggests the culture page has not been refreshed. Environmental and governance claims are largely absent from it.
